items.quote: The world was the first figure or image of God, Man is the image of the World
items.note: Opens a chain of images running downward: God, world, man, animal, zoophite, plant, metals, stones.

items.quote: the Zoophite or sensible hearb is the image of the Animall
items.note: The text names a rank between animal and plant and glosses it as a sensible herb.

items.quote: the prudent Ancients wilsely called Man a Microcosm or little World
items.name: Ancients
items.note: The name Microcosm is given to the Ancients, and the author approves it.

items.quote: which few now a dayes understand, that the great visible World was made Man
items.note: The author says the meaning of the name is understood by few in his day; the sense he gives is that the visible world was made man.

items.quote: so also the little world man is twofold, visible in respect of his Body, invisible in respect of his Spirit
items.what: the little world man is twofold
items.note: Man is divided in two, matching the great world's visible and invisible parts.

items.quote: one a syderiall Spirit from the Firmament, the other from the breath of life
items.note: Two spirits are set apart by their origin: the Firmament and the breath of life.

items.quote: the other from the breath of life, which is the Intellectuall Soul inspired from God, and the mouth of the most High
items.note: The breath of life is said to be the Intellectual Soul inspired from God.

items.quote: Man hath three parts, a mortall Body with a Syderiall Spirit, and an immortall Soule
items.note: Right after two-fold and two-spirit divisions, man is counted in three parts; the Syderiall Spirit goes with the mortal body.

items.quote: an immortall Soule, which is the cottage of the Image of God or of the holy Spirit in Man
items.note: The immortal Soul is defined as the cottage (dwelling) of God's Image or the holy Spirit in man.

items.quote: The first Spirit is from the Limbus or greater world; the second from the word Fiat.
items.note: The margin glosses Limbus as the greater world and sets the second spirit's origin in the word Fiat.

items.quote: Angelicall according to which he is to live, and Animall which is not to be regarded
items.note: The margin divides wisdom in man into Angelical (to be lived by) and Animal (to be disregarded).

items.quote: Regeneration overcometh a bad birth.
items.note: The margin states that regeneration overcomes a bad birth; the lines given do not say what regeneration is here.

items.quote: If a man live sensually by his own proper and proud Will according to flesh and blood onely, he is but a Brute or Beast
items.note: First of three grades of living: sensual living makes a man only a beast.

items.quote: according to those Epithites in Scripture
items.name: Scripture
items.note: The animal names for the sensual man (Dog, Fox, Wolfe, Sheep, Sow, generation of Vipers) are given as Scripture's epithets.

items.quote: of which I shall discourse more at large in my Treatise of Signatures
items.note: The author points to his own Treatise of Signatures for more on this and defers the subject.

items.quote: If he live Rationally, then he is a Man
items.note: Second grade: rational living makes him a man, with dominion over the living creatures in his body.

items.quote: and hath dominion over the living Creatures in his body
items.note: Interpreted: 'living Creatures in his body' points to a second sense, creatures said to be inside man; the lines given do not say what they are.

items.quote: The invisible or immortall body of Man from the breath of God is not subject to Stars or Astronomers.
items.note: The margin exempts the invisible, immortal body from the stars.

items.quote: then hath he dominion over the Stars and all things else
items.note: Third grade: living by the God-like Spirit gives dominion over the stars and all things.

items.quote: if (I say) he live according to the Talent and Treasure laid up in his Earthen Vessell and committed to him
items.note: Figurative words (Tree of Life, Talent, Treasure, Earthen Vessell) stand for what man lives by; the text does not say plainly what the treasure is.

items.quote: He was made of the world, he beareth the world about in him, and is borne of the world.
items.note: Man is made of, carries and is born of the world.

items.quote: the first matter (which was a kind of ineffigiate confused Essence, which Phylosophers call the Chaos and Hylen, or Mother of the world) was the seed of the great world
items.note: The first matter is defined as a shapeless confused Essence and named the seed of the great world.

items.quote: which Phylosophers call the Chaos and Hylen, or Mother of the world
items.name: Phylosophers
items.note: The names Chaos, Hylen and Mother of the world are given to the Philosophers.

items.quote: so the great world is the seed of Adam or Man
items.note: As first matter is to the world, so the world is to man: a chain of seeds.

items.quote: so Man (Adam) lay hid in the world
items.note: Man is said to have lain hidden in the world, as the world lay hidden in the invisible Waters; hidden here as contained before being brought forth.

items.quote: The first matter was made a world, and the great World was made Man.
items.note: States the two steps: first matter to world, world to man.

items.quote: for in every graine or seed of the Tree there lies hid another Tree
items.note: The seed comparison: a whole tree lies hidden in each seed.

items.quote: which Paracelsus calleth the Limbus, whose Earth was the WORD of the Lord
items.name: Paracelsus
items.note: The name Limbus for the First Matter is given to Paracelsus; its Earth is said to be the WORD of the Lord.

items.quote: So the First Matter (which Paracelsus calleth the Limbus, whose Earth was the WORD of the Lord) was the seed of all things that were to be created
items.note: Here Limbus is the First Matter, the seed of the world; N101 glosses Limbus as 'the greater world', which MICRO.17 says the first matter was made into.

items.quote: and Man was the last of all as the perfect seed, which againe is able out of himselfe to beget another Man like himself
items.note: Man is the last and perfect seed, able to beget another like himself.

items.quote: And though Man be not a seed as other seed is, yet hath he power to cast seed out of himselfe
items.note: The text itself says man is not a seed in the ordinary sense: 'seed' is used in a second sense here.

items.quote: all men are but one man, of flesh, blood, and spirit
items.note: Every man born of Adam carries the whole world as Adam did; all men are one man.

items.quote: Therefore the knowledge of Man is to be taken from both Lights, as the Son cannot be known from himselfe alone but from his Father
items.note: Man is known from two Lights, as a son from his father; the two Lights are not named in this sentence.

items.quote: Man hath two Fathers, an Eternall whose Image he beareth, and a Mortall one, which is the whole world with all the creatures
items.note: Man's two fathers: the eternal one and the mortal one, which is the whole world.

items.quote: that is, that Limus Terrae, that slime of the earth, or hidden Secret thing
items.note: The mortal father, the whole world, is glossed as Limus Terrae, slime of the earth.

items.quote: that slime of the earth, or hidden Secret thing
items.note: The Limus Terrae is called a hidden Secret thing.

items.quote: the most precious Esse or Being of all creatures, which all Phylosophers, Physitians Astronomers, and Divines are to consider and diligently inquire into
items.note: The same thing is called the precious Esse of all creatures, and all learned callings are told to inquire into it.

items.quote: In the lesser world Man there is no member or part that doth not answer to some Element, some Planet, some Intelligence or other
items.note: Each part of man corresponds to an element, a planet, an intelligence.

items.quote: to some measure and number in the Archetype or first pattern
items.note: Archetype is glossed as first pattern.

items.quote: Aetheriall and Astrall Body or chariot and vehicle of the Soule, wherein the Intellectuall Soul and earthy Body like two Extreams are knit, glued and confederate together
items.note: Between visible body and intellectual soul stands a third, ethereal and astral body, called chariot and vehicle of the Soul, that joins the two.

items.quote: Water is the Matrix of the world, upon which the Spirit of God moved, Gen. 1.
items.name: Gen. 1
items.note: The margin sets the invisible Waters beside Genesis 1 and 2 Peter 3.5 and calls Water the Matrix of the world.

items.quote: so God extracted every creature out of the first matter
items.note: The margin likens creation to a craftsman shaping many forms; God drew every creature out of the first matter.

items.quote: As the Son is not lesser then his Father, so Man is not lesser then the World.
items.note: The margin calls man the field holding all seeds and no less than the world.

items.quote: None can know the image unlesse he first know him whose image he is.
items.note: The margin: to know man as image, one must first know whose image he is.

items.quote: Hermes calleth Man an earthly God.
items.name: Hermes
items.note: The name 'earthly God' for man is given to Hermes, with Gen. 2.7 beside it.

items.quote: The perfection and dignity of Man.
items.what: The perfection and dignity of Man
items.note: A margin heading marks the passage on the third, astral body as the perfection and dignity of man.

items.quote: is first poured and descendeth into the middle poynt of the Heart, which is the Centre of the little world
items.note: Through the ethereal body, the soul descends first into the heart, named the centre of the little world.

items.quote: by which heat it joyneth to the Spirit begotten from the heart, by the spirit it drencheth it selfe into the blood, by the blood it cleaveth to all the members
items.note: The order of joining: vehicle, natural heat, spirit of the heart, blood, members.

items.quote: whose operations it draweth to it selfe by a peculiar magnetick vertue, just as the visible body doth the efficacy of the Elements
items.note: The ethereal body draws the Firmament's operations by a magnetic virtue, as the visible body draws the elements'.

items.quote: The whole Firmament is in us with the Planets and Stars
items.note: The Firmament with its planets and stars is said to be within man.

items.quote: so that of the syderiall spirit of the Firmament we may learn all Naturall things
items.note: Knowledge of all natural things is to be learned from the syderial spirit.

items.quote: Thus God and Man cannot be united but by a Mean, even our Saviour who partaketh of two Natures
items.note: The margin draws a parallel: as the ethereal body is the mean in man, so the Saviour is the mean between God and man.

items.quote: is infused by God into the Elementary body through the Astra's as a Medium
items.name: Paracelsus
items.note: The descent of the soul through the Astra's as a medium is given as Paracelsus's saying.

items.quote: John 10.30.
items.name: John 10.30
items.note: A scripture reference stands beside 'as the Son with his Father'.

items.quote: The MIND.
items.note: A margin heading names the passage on learning all natural things from the syderial spirit as the MIND.

items.quote: The MIND.
items.note: N111 sets 'The MIND' beside the syderial spirit of the Firmament; MICRO.24 has the Spirit or Mind from God and MICRO.25 has God in man's 'Soule or Mind'.

items.quote: with the four foresaid inhabitants of the Elements, which the bruit beasts have not
items.note: Points back to an earlier place where the four inhabitants of the elements were named; that place is not in the lines given.

items.quote: or Spirit by the inbreathing of God, created
items.note: The intellectual, immortal soul or spirit is made by God's inbreathing, after the image of God and the Triunity.

items.quote: from which we learn sacred Divinity and all heavenly and earthly secrets without errour
items.note: From God's Spirit in us all heavenly and earthly secrets are learned without error.

items.name: Zach. 12.1. Gen. 2.7. Es. 42.5. Wisd. 2.23.
items.note: Scripture references stand beside the immortal soul made by God's inbreathing.

items.quote: 1 John 2.27. Chap. 4.14. Acts 17.28.
items.name: 1 John 2.27. Chap. 4.14. Acts 17.28.
items.note: Scripture references stand beside the closing words 'in him we are, and live, and are moved'.

items.quote: As God is One in Essence, Trine (or Three) in persons, so Man is One in Person, Trine (or Three) in distinct Essence
items.note: Man mirrors God inversely: God one essence three persons, man one person three essences.

items.quote: that is, composed Triune, of a Terrene Body, an Aethereall Spirit of the Heavens, and a living vivifying Soule which God breathed into him
items.note: Man's threefold essence is spelled out: earthly body, ethereal spirit, God-breathed soul.

items.quote: This the holy Scripture witnesseth
items.name: holy Scripture
items.note: Scripture is called as witness to man's threefold make.

items.quote: Unitrine or Triune, One in Three, or Three in One
items.note: Unitrine and Triune are glossed as One in Three, Three in One.

items.quote: the unanimous consent of all that truly professed Phylosophy from the Light of Nature
items.name: all that truly professed Phylosophy
items.note: A second witness: the agreement of true philosophers from the Light of Nature.

items.quote: See the Amphi{G075: 1 letter illegible}halce of Rhunrad worthy of perpetuall memory.
items.name: Rhunrad
items.note: The margin points the reader to a work of Rhunrad and praises it.

items.quote: Paul the greatest Phylosopher and Divine shewes three parts of Man, Spirit, Soule and Body.
items.name: Paul
items.note: The three parts are given to Paul, called the greatest philosopher and divine.

items.quote: There are two Souls or two Spirits in Man, Mortall from the first matter which is the life of the body, and Immortall from God.
items.note: The margin derives the mortal spirit from the first matter; MICRO.14 derives the syderial spirit from the Firmament.

items.quote: The Spirit is the Life of the Soule, the Spirit and Soule are the life of the body.
items.note: The margin orders what gives life to what: spirit to soul, spirit and soul to body.

items.quote: Man was created è Limo Terrae, out of the clay or dust of the Earth, by the word FIAT
items.note: è Limo Terrae is glossed as out of the clay or dust of the Earth; set against deniers of the three parts.

items.quote: which is that Linum Caelorum, or slime of the Heavens from the Lord
items.note: The eternal spirit or breath of life is named Linum Caelorum, glossed as slime of the Heavens.

items.quote: The Limus Terrae, or dust of the Earth, is two-fold, visible and invisible
items.note: The dust of the earth is split: the visible body from earth and water, the invisible life from air and fire.

items.quote: which life is the Syderiall Spirit, and is properly the Man, not flesh and blood
items.note: The syderial spirit, not flesh and blood, is properly the man.

items.quote: As the Syderiall Spirit is the life of the Body, so the Spirit of the Lord is the life of the Intellectuall Soule.
items.note: Two parallel lives: syderial spirit for body, Spirit of the Lord for soul.

items.quote: for this invisible is himselfe the Firmament
items.note: The syderial spirit in the body is itself the Firmament and holds all things.

items.quote: so the Spirit of the Lord, the WORD of God, the eternall man dwells in the Soule
items.note: Here the Spirit of the Lord dwelling in the soul is called 'the eternall man'; MICRO.23 says the syderial spirit 'is properly the Man'.

items.quote: the house is the habitation of the Soule, the Soule is the habitation and cottage of God
items.note: Nested dwellings: house for the soul, soul for God.

items.quote: it followeth that there are three worlds or Heavens in Man
items.what: three worlds or Heavens in Man
items.note: From man as the last and fullest work, it follows that three worlds are in him and he is all the world.

items.quote: And therefore some have called him the Fourth World
items.note: A name given to man by unnamed others: the fourth world holding what is in the other three.

items.quote: for what else is the Spirit of Man which God breathed into him but God himselfe dwelling in us?
items.note: The breathed spirit of man is God himself dwelling in us.

items.quote: The invisible Body or true Internall Man consisting of Reason and an Astrall Spirit, agreeth with the Angells, and is their fellow
items.note: The invisible body is the true internal man, made of reason and astral spirit, fellow of the angels.

items.quote: And if he be a true Magician, he is not inferiour to the Angells in all Magicall operation
items.note: A true Magician equals the angels in magical operation and is lord of all things; the lines given do not say what makes one true.

items.quote: for all Externall things are nothing else but the Body of Man
items.note: All external things are called man's body.

items.quote: So that he partaketh of a threefold world, of the Archetype or God-like world in God, of the Intellible or Angellicall, of the sensible Elementall or corporall world
items.note: The three worlds are named: Archetype, Angelical, Elemental.

items.quote: So that he partaketh of a threefold world
items.note: Here man partakes of three worlds; the numbered list that follows gives five things he shares in (God, Angels, Firmament, Elements, animals-plants-minerals).

items.quote: God created Man to be his Tabernacle as well in this as in the world to come.
items.note: The margin: man is God's tabernacle now and hereafter.

items.quote: Exemplumque Dei quisque est in imagine parvâ, Manilus.
items.name: Manilus
items.note: A Latin line given to Manilus stands beside man as pattern of the universe.

items.quote: That which is Naturated savoureth of the Nature of that which did Naturate it.
items.note: The margin: what is made carries the nature of its maker.

items.quote: God dwelleth in the Soul as in the Heaven of Man.
items.note: The margin: the soul is man's heaven where God dwells.

items.quote: He communicateth with God in his Soule or Mind
items.note: First of five numbered ways man shares in the worlds: with God through soul or mind.

items.quote: the Intellectuall Soul is a certaine particle of the Divine Soule
items.note: The intellectual soul is called a particle of the divine soul.

items.quote: God hath sowen certaine seeds and resemblances of his Mind in us, much like to that of an Eccho
items.note: God's mind is in man as sown seeds and resemblances, likened to an echo.

items.quote: The mind raised up into the most High God and united with him converseth with God, and doth the same works
items.note: The raised mind, united with God, does the same works as God.

items.quote: neither is there any thing in God which very thing is not represented in Man
items.note: Everything in God is represented in man.

items.quote: Stern-man of the Soul or Rationall Spirit, & like the eternall God concludeth all Beings, Times and Places
items.note: The margin defines the Mind as driver or steersman of the soul or rational spirit; a word in foreign script before it is a gap.

items.quote: He hath a semblance with the Angells in respect of the invisible Body and Rationall Soul
items.note: Second: with the angels through invisible body and rational soul, sharing their wisdom.

items.quote: for he is Gabalis socius Angelorum, a curdled companion of the Angells, or one mixed with in fellowship
items.note: The Latin phrase is Englished as a curdled companion of the angels.

items.quote: He participateth with the Firmament and Stars of whom he received that Astrall body or Syderiall Spirit, which is the true Astrall Man
items.note: Third: with the Firmament and stars through the astral body, called the true Astral Man.

items.quote: which Astrall Spirit is the subject of humane Reason that containeth the sences and wisdome in it
items.note: The astral spirit is defined as the seat of human reason, holding senses and wisdom.

items.quote: the Astra's rule man in the Spirit, and the Spirit of a man ruleth the Body in flesh and blood
items.note: A chain of rule: the Astra's over the spirit, the spirit over the body; spirit and Astra's are one thing in man.

items.quote: This Spirit is mortall; onely the Intellectuall Soule which God breathed into man is immortall.
items.note: The astral spirit is mortal; only the God-breathed soul is immortal.

items.quote: The invisible or immortall body of Man from the breath of God is not subject to Stars or Astronomers.
items.note: N103 calls the invisible body immortal and free of the stars; MICRO.24 says the invisible body consists of reason and an astral spirit, and MICRO.27 says that spirit is mortal and ruled by the Astra's.

items.quote: He partaketh of the Elements, for from these he had his mortall Physicall Earthy body
items.note: Fourth: with the elements, source of the mortal body.

items.quote: the world, which is the Parant of Man according to Paracelsus
items.name: Paracelsus
items.note: The world as man's parent is given to Paracelsus.

items.quote: hath in it the four Elementary Spirits of the four inhabitants of the world, as also the fift kind of Flages of a thousand sorts
items.what: the four Elementary Spirits ... the fift kind of Flages
items.note: Five kinds of spirits are named: four of the elements' inhabitants and a fifth called Flages; the lines given do not say what Flages are.

items.quote: the Imagination also of these five Spirits in the Elements must be in the Microcosm Man
items.note: The five spirits' imagination is in man.

items.quote: the use of Mans Reason according to the will and command of God, is as a Chaine were with those five Spirits are knit and bound together
items.note: Reason used by God's command binds the five spirits so they yield to man's imagination.

items.quote: He partaketh of all Elemented Animalls, Vegetables and Mineralls
items.note: Fifth: with animals, plants and minerals, whose natures he holds.

items.quote: Man therefore who was the last is the most excellent and noble of all Creatures, because he hath the parts of the whole world
items.note: Conclusion: as last made and holding the whole world, man is the noblest creature.

items.quote: The Son is like the father in all things, the father being known the Son is known also.
items.note: The father-son likeness again: knowing the world (the father) gives knowledge of man.

items.quote: most admirable Extract & kernell of the four Elements
items.what: Extract & kernell of the four Elements
items.note: Man is named the extract and kernel of the elements, words from separating a thing's best part.

items.quote: Yea he riseth to such perfection that he is made the Son of God, transformed into the same image which is God and made one with him
items.note: Man can rise to become Son of God, one with God.

items.quote: which is not granted either to Angells, or the world, or any other Creature, but to Man only
items.note: This union with God is granted to man alone, not to angels.

items.quote: All things were made of nothing and Man was made of all those things.
items.note: The margin: man made of all things, the great world the matrix of Adam.

items.name: John 17.11, 12.22, 23
items.note: Scripture references stand beside man made one with God.
